---
title: "juphyter"
subtitle: "A Jupyter and Quarto kernel for PHP"
jupyter: php
---

Run PHP in Jupyter notebooks and Quarto documents, with tables and charts
displayed alongside code.

A notebook is a file of cells, each holding a few lines of code with its
output beneath it. The program that runs the cells is a kernel. juphyter is a
kernel for PHP, and it keeps one PHP session open, so a variable set in one
cell is available in the next.

- **JupyterLab:** after `juphyter install`, JupyterLab lists PHP in its
  launcher. See [JupyterLab](jupyter.qmd).
- **Quarto:** a `.qmd` that names `jupyter: php` in its front matter renders
  its `{php}` cells to HTML, PDF, or Word. See [Quarto](quarto.qmd).

## What a cell shows

The value of a cell's last expression is its output. A
[phibble](https://phibble.phpstats.org) data frame appears as an HTML table
with its dimensions and column types, and a
[phiz](https://phiz.phpstats.org) plot appears as a chart. Other values appear
as a compact dump.

The examples below use phibble, phplyr, and phiz. In a Composer project,
install them with the command below. The `php` kernel then loads the
project's `vendor/autoload.php` for any notebook or document inside the
project. [The phpstats packages](install.qmd#the-phpstats-packages) covers
using them outside a project.

```bash
composer require phpstats/phibble phpstats/phplyr phpstats/phiz
```

phplyr's `round()` replaces PHP's built-in `round()` in the cells after this
import.

```{php}
use function Phplyr\{phplyr, group_by, summarize, arrange, desc, n, mean, round};
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="syntax"}

## PHP 8.5+

```{php}
$mpg = \Phibble\DataFrame::fromRows(\Phiz\Datasets::mpg());

$mpg |>
    group_by('class') |>
    summarize(models: n(), hwy: round(mean('hwy'), 1)) |>
    arrange(desc('hwy'));
```

## PHP 8.3–8.4

```{php}
$mpg = \Phibble\DataFrame::fromRows(\Phiz\Datasets::mpg());

phplyr($mpg)
    ->groupBy('class')
    ->summarize(models: n(), hwy: round(mean('hwy'), 1))
    ->arrange(desc('hwy'))
    ->get();
```

:::

```{php}
#| fig-cap: "Highway mileage against engine displacement."
\Phiz\Plot::of(\Phiz\Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point(opacity: 0.7)
    ->smooth(method: 'lm')
    ->labs(x: 'Displacement (L)', y: 'Highway mpg', color: 'Drive');
```

## What the kernel provides

- State across cells, including `use` imports and declared functions and
  classes.
- Tracebacks that name the cell and the line, instead of `eval()'d code`.
- HTML tables for phibble data frames and charts for phiz plots, plus
  `toHtml()` and `toMimeBundle()` hooks for any other class.
- `Juphyter\display()`, which shows a value part way through a cell.
- Completion of variables, functions, classes, and members.
- Interrupting a running cell with the stop button, when PHP has the `pcntl`
  extension.
- Loading the nearest `vendor/autoload.php` above the notebook, so a notebook
  inside a Composer project can use that project's classes and packages.

juphyter requires none of the phpstats packages. It runs plain PHP, and it
formats a phibble data frame or a phiz plot when those packages are
installed.

## How it works

A Python program built on [ipykernel](https://github.com/ipython/ipykernel)
handles the Jupyter protocol, and a PHP process runs the cells. They talk over
a Unix socket. That is why an install needs Python as well as PHP, and why the
kernel runs on macOS and Linux only.
